what: The first end-to-end run at a width only the folded pair table can hold: K_0/GF(2^61), a 48-bit subgroup, 300608 base points in 2464 signed orbits. All four stages, 32 of 32 targets verified against a signed-Frobenius rho baseline.

the_ab_that_matters.what: The same parameter file and the same base, run twice on binaries differing only by the orbit tag and the row filter. The relation counts came back identical unit for unit -- 18347, 18363, 18394, 18391 -- which is a stronger cross-check that the tagged, row-filtered table answers exactly as the untagged one than any unit test: a whole pipeline agreeing to the relation.

peak_rss_gib.note: the row filter halves the stored pairs, and it shows in resident memory

the_ab_that_matters.why_the_before_was_slow: Collection spent 11.85 ms a probe, which is about one O(|F|) recovery scan per probe at this width -- precisely the cost the orbit tag removes. The first run's binary predated it.

against_the_previous_best_at_this_degree.the_honest_qualification: Amortised over 32 targets the folded width is WORSE: 0.45 against 1.288. The base has 8.3 times as many points and so 8.3 times as many orbits to solve logarithms for, and the precompute grew from 79.0 s to 235.7 s. A wider base buys a cheaper descent and charges for it once, up front.
against_the_previous_best_at_this_degree.break_even_reading: With the collection sized to the columns, the folded width overtakes the 36112-point compact one at about 1812 targets: the extra 77.9 s of precompute divided by the 0.0430 s a target the descent saves. It was 3635 before the sizing. Below that the narrower base wins. This remains the clearest statement of what the work is: a method for many logarithms on one curve, and never for one.

not_claimed: That the folded width is better at every scale. At 32 targets it is not, and the amortised ratio says so. The charged ratio and the break-even count are the claims.

sized_to_the_columns.what: The first run collected 73495 relations to certify 2464 columns -- a thirtyfold oversupply -- and spent 87.6 s of the logs stage verifying all of them, against 0.088 s for the solve. The units were inherited from the 36112-point file, where a probe yielded far less.
sized_to_the_columns.how_it_was_sized: Each relation touches three orbits, so covering every column needs about cols*ln(cols)/3 = 6414 relations before any margin for independence. At the measured 0.919 relations a probe, 14000 probes should give about 12900, a margin of 1.8. It gave 12843, and all 2464 columns certified with 0 rejected -- so the margin is sized, not lucky.

charged.note: unchanged within noise, as it should be -- sizing the collection does not touch the descent

sized_to_the_columns.a_contaminated_measurement_discarded: A first attempt at this gave collect 137.9 s and amortised 0.56. The test suite was run during that stage's pair-table build, so the stage total was contended; the unit times were clean and scaled correctly with the probe count. It was re-run with nothing else on the machine and those are the numbers above.

where_precompute_goes_now.pair_table_build: about 102 s of the 107.1 s collect stage
where_precompute_goes_now.reading: The sparse solve is 0.029 s -- 0.02% of precompute. The block Wiedemann work this repo did earlier is no longer anywhere near the cost. What precompute is made of at this width is the pair-table build and verifying relations in the general group arithmetic.
